resources.string: Automatically populates fields with real-world developer scenarios like GitHub PRs or Server Alerts.\n\nSmart Logic: If Multiline or Big Text is enabled, the app automatically selects longer payloads to fill the view. Manual input is locked while active.
Uses a fixed ID (0). New notifications will replace the previous one in the drawer. Turn this OFF if you want to test notification stacking or grouped bundles.
Sets the \"Ongoing\" flag. On older devices, it prevents swiping. Note: On Android 14+, users can still swipe these away unless a Foreground Service is active.

A UI-only convenience that expands the input field on the main screen for easier typing. \n\nImportant: The actual notification text will still be truncated by the OS unless the Big Text Style is also enabled.

Simulates high-interruption events like Alarms or Incoming Calls. If the screen is locked and permission is granted, the app UI will launch immediately upon arrival.

Smart Logic: Importance is forced to "Urgent" and unique IDs are used to bypass system-level restrictions.

Note: By design, the Android System UI may hide navigation buttons (Recents/Home) during a Full-Screen Intent to prevent accidental clicks. Standard navigation returns once the device is securely unlocked.

Tip: Use a sending delay to allow time to lock your device. For 100%% success on some manufacturers, set Battery to "Unrestricted" and ensure "Display over other apps" is allowed.

Bundles multiple notifications into a stack using a Group Key. 

Smart Logic: When active, the "Overwrite" setting is automatically ignored and unique IDs are used so you can see the bundling effect. 

Tip: Send 2 or 3 notifications in a row to see the group summary header appear.
Starts a continuous loop at the chosen interval. This is used for stress-testing notification arrival and verifying background stability over long periods.
Applies a timer before firing the notification. Perfect for testing how the device behaves when the app is in the background or the screen is turned off.
Allows the notification to expand into a large block of text. This tool uses a %1$d-character teaser in the collapsed view to ensure the expansion arrow remains visible.
Displays a large hero image when expanded. Note: This tool automatically converts XML icons to Bitmaps and uses a 2:1 padding ratio to prevent cropping on modern devices.
Formats the notification as a list of individual lines. This tool automatically chunks long text into separate lines, as Inbox Style does not support text wrapping.
Adds interactive buttons (like STOP) to the notification card. Use this to test user engagement and the execution of PendingIntents from the drawer.
Supplementary header metadata. This tool combines the App Name and Hint using a bullet point. Note: Some modern OS versions hide this to save vertical space.
Adds a circular thumbnail image. Note: While standard Android shows this on the right, Xiaomi HyperOS typically displays it on the left.
Adds a live, system-managed timer that counts up from the moment of arrival. Ideal for testing Call UIs or active background tasks.
Controls haptic feedback. Used to verify that silent notification channels or \"Do Not Disturb\" exceptions are behaving correctly.
Toggles the default system notification sound. Tests if the channel importance correctly triggers an audible alert on the device.
Maps to Android Channels. Urgent (Heads-up banner), High (Sound), Medium (No sound), and Low (Silent/Minimized). Note: Importance is locked once a channel is created.

Determines how much content is shown when the device is locked.

• Public: Shows all content (Title, Body, Images).
• Private: Shows the app icon but hides the message content.
• Secret: Hides the notification completely until the device is unlocked.

Note: System-level privacy settings and a lack of a screen lock (PIN/Biometric) will override these choices.
